summary.intent: Clear a large backlog of open issues on the CipherBox v2 repo by identifying parallelizable work, batching issues into PRs grouped by non-overlapping file ownership, and driving them through implementation, review (CodeRabbit/macroscope), and merge with minimal CodeRabbit-quota waste — including overnight/AFK operation and cleanup of stale tracking-issue references in code comments.
summary.outcome: Merged roughly a dozen PRs closing ~40+ issues across multiple waves, decomposed the blocked #635 rotation epic into schedulable sub-issues with dependency edges, wrote 2 ADRs to formalize sweep/name-wave design decisions, restored branch protection on main, added a merge-blocking 'Tracker Refs' CI gate that removed 449 stale issue references (91% pointing to closed issues) across 131 files, and fixed multiple latent security/correctness bugs (constant-time comparison gaps, rule-8 encode/decode asymmetries, epoch-mismatch signing bugs, resource-cap bypasses) surfaced by review gates along the way.

repo: cargo fmt --all and cargo check --workspace never build the wasm32 target — a separate `cargo test -p X --target wasm32-wasip1` run is required to catch usize-width bugs (usize is 4 bytes on wasm32, causing copy_from_slice panics invisible to native tests)

AGENTS.md rule 8 requires decode-side hard rejects to have a release-active encode-side Err, never debug_assert! — violated and caught multiple times (grant section unknown-field collision, RecordTooLarge, ascentLink absence)
GitHub Actions staging deploy vars are split: some live at repo scope, some at 'staging' environment scope; jobs without `environment:` (e.g. web-e2e.yml) only see repo-scope vars

CodeRabbit posts clean verdicts by editing the status comment in place (login `coderabbitai[bot]`); findings are posted as a separate submitted review body — pollers must check both surfaces with a startswith login match and a since-timestamp fence

CodeRabbit dedupes reviews by head SHA — an incremental 'already reviewed' state (even from just a walkthrough) blocks re-review of that SHA; `@coderabbitai full review` is the override but is itself fair-usage rate-limited
macroscope reviews were initially triggered on draft PRs (unlike CodeRabbit); user later disabled draft review so all three reviewers (CodeRabbit, Greptile, macroscope) are now ready-gated

docs/adr/ in cipher-box is dead v1 residue (last touched 2026-06-28, describes retired AES-256-GCM); the live ADR mechanism is FSM1/cipher-box-next/decisions/, used only when a decision amends/extends a frozen wayfinder issue decision

Two-digit `#NN` refs in code (e.g. `#33 D6`) are cipher-box-next wayfinder decision citations, never cipher-box issue numbers — cipher-box's issue counter jumped from #71 (2026-02) directly to #300+, so the two-digit namespace is permanently unambiguous
facade.rs, tests/write_plane.rs, sync/drain.rs, and gate/floor.rs are perpetual hot-file contention points across nearly every engine PR wave
tools/hw-gates is a standalone cargo workspace not covered by the root `cargo fmt --all`
main branch had zero branch protection until this session (only a tag-immutability ruleset existed) — the 'passing checks' UI was purely informational

code.finding: Carried history links must be re-signed at the current read epoch on republish, not copied verbatim — original bug meant rotating a scope twice made it permanently unadoptable; fix truncates to the walkable suffix rather than Err on gaps, to avoid a denial-of-revocation vector
usize-width KAT generation bug: b.tag[..8].copy_from_slice(&i.to_be_bytes()) with i: usize panics on wasm32 (4-byte usize) — fixed via (i as u64).to_be_bytes()

floor::check rejects epoch < epoch_floor; a scope root can never legitimately be below its own floor since rotate/cascade always publish before raising the floor — this invalidated #1025's original SweepResolver premise
ChildRef.ipns_name lives in the parent's read body — a write-plane name wave must rewrite every parent's child refs or read-only grantees get stranded, per ADR 0004

workflow: When scheduling recurring/timed jobs, always use absolute epoch seconds (date -u +%s), never HH:MM string comparisons — a numeric-string compare bug ([ "2336" -ge "0131" ]) fired jobs early and burned review slots

Verify every claim from a completed agent against the actual code/diff before relaying it to the user — caught false 'already fixed' and 'unreachable code' claims, and self-corrected several times mid-session

Build the actual merge (git merge + cargo check/test in a scratch worktree) rather than reasoning about line-number diffs to detect semantic merge conflicts — predicted conflicts that didn't materialize and vice versa

Never apply a code-review suggestion literally — twice a suggested fix (Err on unwalkable chain, durable in-doubt marking) would have introduced a worse bug (denial-of-revocation, moved-not-removed failure window) than the one reported
Nohup'd background jobs survive but are not harness-tracked and never trigger notifications — always use tracked background tasks instead

Use worktree-isolated agents with explicit file-ownership boundaries to parallelize PR work safely, and always run a pairwise + N-way combined merge+compile+test verification before flipping any PR ready
Patching branch protection required_status_checks is a full-list PATCH, not additive — always fetch and diff the existing list before writing

friction: Lost ~1 hour of overnight review throughput due to a scheduling bug (HH:MM numeric string comparison) that fired two ready-flips inside the CodeRabbit rate-limit window

Spent significant time misdiagnosing CodeRabbit's non-response on #1065 (three wrong theories: SHA dedup, daily cap, quota) before discovering the poller's login-string filter (`coderabbitai` vs `coderabbitai[bot]`) was blind to the clean-verdict status-comment surface the whole time
Retry loop for #1065 (`@coderabbitai review`/`full review`) overwrote the clean verdict in the mutable status comment, destroying the evidence the user later had to supply via screenshot
GitHub API connectivity flapped repeatedly (connection refused) throughout the session, causing several failed pushes/polls requiring retry logic

Agent doing #1046 fix used --no-verify assuming a Rust-only diff, but the diff actually included blueprint/engine.md with 4 real markdownlint violations that CI would never have caught (lint:md not wired into any workflow)
One sweep agent overstepped scope and degraded two-digit wayfinder decision citations it was told to leave alone, requiring manual revert and audit
